summary: Fix all 32 deduplicated backup/demo review findings and integration regressions without moving pool work or state into Controller

guide.reason: Operator instructions now preserve exact repository retry bodies, clear pool-bound drafts, explain unresolved work and resumable forgetting, distinguish safe retained-TPM admission from legacy uncertainty, and describe current member eligibility, independent history loading and bounded deployment uploads.

api.reason: Pinned current-master Core peer GET retain uses count/byte-bounded after_id pages and complete exact member snapshots; targeted snapshot POST retain/forget replaces negative-list deletion. Orphan-cleanup authority uses bounded per-point framing. Updated peers and a fresh complete replica are required. Client-facing registration, backup, restore, retained-release and policy payloads are unchanged; existing authorization, receipt replay, interrupted rollback, uncertainty and exact-retry behavior are corrected.

roadmap.reason: Review bug fixes do not close a milestone or certify native storage, recovery, fencing or publication workflows.

state.reason: All pool definitions, outcomes and recovery intent remain durable on Core; Controller stores no new pool state. Mutation reservations and live-worker tracking are transient exclusion only.
state.record: The pool master's existing backup repository registry, operation receipts, run/policy/catalog/pin/orphan records and signed complete authority replicas. Individual Core hosts separately retain sealed credentials and host-local pending-detach snapshots; these are not part of the authority stream. Executing-host managed journals persist exact retained_tpm admission before deletion. A fresh Controller connects to the master and adopts members, inventory and authenticated host outcomes with unchanged identities; host-local release results remain available without the old Controller database.

verification.method: Run focused and integrated Go race regressions, shared UI typecheck/tests/build, API generation/contract checks, documentation/privacy gates, actual compiled demo/API browser workflow, fictional-API operator browser failure/retry/scope scenarios, receiver subprocess smoke and isolated root filesystem rollback. Actual results and simulation limits are recorded in the QA report; no real storage, remote CI, publication or history cleanup is claimed.
